D_policy_objective: Completely replaces the 2001 fisheries law (Lei n.º 9/2001) with a comprehensive legal framework for the sustainable conservation, exploitation and management of aquatic and marine (haliêutico) resources under national jurisdiction, providing the legal foundation for the Ecosystem Approach to Fisheries (EAF) and for marine protected areas (Chapter III). The law contains no explicit mention of 'plástico'/'plastic' by name, but functions as an important indirect marine-plastics instrument through: (i) an explicit prohibition on the abandonment of 'non-biodegradable' fishing gear and fish-aggregating/concentration devices in national maritime waters (Art. 139(1)(c)) — a direct Abandoned, Lost or Discarded Fishing Gear (ALDFG) provision, ALDFG being one of the most significant and persistent sources of ocean plastic pollution worldwide; (ii) a general duty prohibiting fishing-related activities from polluting or degrading coastal and marine ecosystems (Art. 22); (iii) prohibitions on discharging hydrocarbons and other toxic/hazardous substances, and on transhipping toxic or radioactive materials, into national maritime waters, classified as 'very serious' fishing infractions (Art. 137(1)(g) and (j)); (iv) a civil liability regime for environmental damage caused by dumping waste or toxic chemicals into aquatic environments (Arts. 142-146); and (v) regulation of vessel/gear conduct, at-sea works and liquid-waste discharges, and aquaculture effluents. The law was subsequently amended and republished by Lei n.º 7/2025 (29 December 2025), which — per FAO's Development Law Service — clarified definitions, revised the sanctions regime (indexing fines to the civil-service minimum wage for automatic adjustment), and extended the sanctions scheme to infractions arising under a new General Regulation on Fishing Activities (covering subsistence and recreational fishing) that was still pending presidential promulgation as of that report.
H_policy_type_justification: Act of Parliament — 'A Assembleia Nacional decreta, nos termos da alínea b) do artigo 97.º da Constituição, o seguinte' / 'The National Assembly decrees, under paragraph (b) of Article 97 of the Constitution, the following.' Subsequently amended and republished by Lei n.º 7/2025, de 29 de Dezembro — also an Act of the National Assembly. Both are primary legislation, not executive decrees or regulations (the law itself contemplates further executive 'Regulamento Geral das Actividades de Pesca' and other regulations, e.g. Arts. 13-14, but these are subsidiary instruments, not coded here as they were not made available for this exercise).

N_policy_budget_text: Art. 70.º: 'O Fundo de Desenvolvimento das Pescas... tem a finalidade de contribuir com recursos financeiros para o desenvolvimento do sector das pescas.' / 'The Fisheries Development Fund... has the purpose of contributing financial resources to the development of the fisheries sector.' Art. 71.º(1): the Fund's financial resources include: '(a) Financiamento directo do Orçamento Geral do Estado; (b) Fundos de organismos internacionais; (c) Percentagem consignada das receitas não fiscais, nos termos legais; (d) Percentagem das coimas e indemnizações aplicadas ao abrigo do presente Diploma; (e) Contribuição de empresas e pessoas singulares; (f) Totalidade de apoio institucional de pescas no âmbito dos acordos de parceria de pesca; (g) Outros fundos legalmente admitidos.' / '(a) direct financing from the General State Budget; (b) funds from international organisations; (c) an earmarked percentage of non-tax revenue, under legal terms; (d) a percentage of fines and compensation applied under this Decree; (e) contributions from companies and individuals; (f) the totality of institutional fisheries support under fisheries partnership agreements; (g) other legally admissible funds.' Art. 150.º further provides that fine proceeds not otherwise allocated revert to State coffers, with a percentage share for maritime-safety and rescue institutions, as defined by joint ministerial order.
R_instrument_description: Art. 139.º(1)(c): 'Constituem infracções de pesca graves previstas na lei e regulamentos: ... c) Abandono de artes e dispositivos de concentração não biodegradáveis nas águas marítimas nacionais.' / 'The following constitute serious fishing infractions under this law and its regulations: ... (c) Abandonment of non-biodegradable gear and concentration devices [e.g. fish-aggregating devices, FADs] in national maritime waters.' Punished under Art. 139.º(2): fines of Dbs. 2,500.00 to Dbs. 25,000.00 for artisanal fishing vessels; Dbs. 10,000.00 to Dbs. 50,000.00 for semi-industrial vessels; and Dbs. 1,000,000.00 to Dbs. 5,000,000.00 for industrial vessels.
U_instrument_implementation_text: Authority: Art. 73.º(3) vests primary competence for enforcement of this Law's provisions in the 'autoridade competente' (competent fisheries authority) (+0.25). Enforcement: Art. 139.º(2)'s explicit, tiered fine schedule by vessel category (+0.25). Monitoring: Art. 87.º(1)(b) empowers fisheries inspectors/agents to 'Ordenar que lhes sejam mostradas as redes, bem como as capturas a bordo e às artes de pesca' / 'order that nets, catches on board and fishing gear be shown to them', extending general surveillance to gear on board and, by implication, gear disposal practices (+0.25). Unconditional: no exemption is stated for this prohibition (+0.25).
W_comments: Instrument type: Regulatory (1). THE MOST DIRECTLY PLASTICS-RELEVANT PROVISION IN THIS LAW: 'não biodegradáveis' (non-biodegradable) fishing gear and fish-aggregating/concentration devices are, in practice, overwhelmingly made of synthetic plastic materials (nylon/polyethylene netting, polypropylene rope, plastic FAD floats and rafts). This provision is a direct Abandoned, Lost or Discarded Fishing Gear (ALDFG) prohibition — ALDFG is recognised internationally (e.g. by FAO and UNEP) as one of the most harmful and persistent forms of ocean plastic pollution. Satisfies plastics-relevance criterion (b) directly (an instrument enabling action against a major plastic-pollution source) and arguably (a) by clear functional equivalence, even though the word 'plástico' is not used.

D_policy_objective: Completely replaces the 2001 fisheries law (Lei n.º 9/2001) with a comprehensive legal framework for the sustainable conservation, exploitation and management of aquatic and marine (haliêutico) resources under national jurisdiction, providing the legal foundation for the Ecosystem Approach to Fisheries (EAF) and for marine protected areas (Chapter III). The law contains no explicit mention of 'plástico'/'plastic' by name, but functions as an important indirect marine-plastics instrument through: (i) an explicit prohibition on the abandonment of 'non-biodegradable' fishing gear and fish-aggregating/concentration devices in national maritime waters (Art. 139(1)(c)) — a direct Abandoned, Lost or Discarded Fishing Gear (ALDFG) provision, ALDFG being one of the most significant and persistent sources of ocean plastic pollution worldwide; (ii) a general duty prohibiting fishing-related activities from polluting or degrading coastal and marine ecosystems (Art. 22); (iii) prohibitions on discharging hydrocarbons and other toxic/hazardous substances, and on transhipping toxic or radioactive materials, into national maritime waters, classified as 'very serious' fishing infractions (Art. 137(1)(g) and (j)); (iv) a civil liability regime for environmental damage caused by dumping waste or toxic chemicals into aquatic environments (Arts. 142-146); and (v) regulation of vessel/gear conduct, at-sea works and liquid-waste discharges, and aquaculture effluents. The law was subsequently amended and republished by Lei n.º 7/2025 (29 December 2025), which — per FAO's Development Law Service — clarified definitions, revised the sanctions regime (indexing fines to the civil-service minimum wage for automatic adjustment), and extended the sanctions scheme to infractions arising under a new General Regulation on Fishing Activities (covering subsistence and recreational fishing) that was still pending presidential promulgation as of that report.
